# Ghar Raksha

> Ghar Raksha is a free, open DIY home-security project for Pakistani homes.
> An ESP32 board reads PIR, microwave radar (RCWL-0516), mmWave (HLK-LD2410)
> and magnetic door sensors (MC-38), sounds a siren, turns on a light, and
> sends a Telegram alert when someone enters an armed zone. A web dashboard
> shows a live radar map of the house and can arm/disarm the system.
> It does NOT depend on CCTV: a thief can dodge a camera, but sensors do not
> need a face, only a body. The project is written in Roman Urdu + simple
> English. All code, wiring guide and shopping list are on this site, free.

## Pages

- [Home](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/): what the system is, how it works in 5 steps, zones, costs, honest limits, FAQ.
- [Radar Dashboard](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/dashboard): live radar map of the house, 4 zones, arm/disarm, alert log. DEMO MODE shows simulated data; LIVE MODE connects to the ESP32 over the local WiFi (/status, /arm, /disarm).
- [Apna Map Banao / Map Editor](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/map-editor): build your own authentic house map (rooms, courtyard, gate) on a 100x100 grid and save it in the browser (localStorage key gharRaksha.map.v1). The dashboard then shows your map instead of the default one, in DEMO and LIVE mode.
- [Setup Guide](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/setup): step-by-step wiring (pin tables matching the firmware exactly), code upload via Arduino IDE, dashboard connection, zone testing, nightly arming routine.
- [Shopping List](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/shopping): parts with Pakistan prices checked 25 Nov 2026 (digilog.pk, Daraz.pk, robochacha.pk, mreeco.com, circuithub.pk).
- [Downloads](https://ghar-raksha.pages.dev/downloads): ESP32 firmware source (home_guard.ino) and pre-compiled firmware.bin + bootloader.bin + partitions.bin with esptool flash command.

## Map Editor (Apna Map Banao)

The default dashboard map is one house (Kamra 1, Kamra 2, Sehan, Main Gate).
Every house is different, so each user can draw their own authentic map in
the editor: name each zone, pick its type (Kamra / Sehan / Main Gate / Bahar /
Aur), place it on a 100x100 grid by tapping the canvas or typing numbers.
Saving writes {houseName, zones:[{name,type,x,y,w,h}]} to localStorage; the
dashboard loads it on start and uses those zones (names, rectangles, types)
for the map, zone list, demo walk and alert log. A corrupt or missing save
falls back to the default map, so the dashboard never breaks.

## Costs (Pakistan, prices checked 25 Nov 2026)

- Starter, 1 zone: ~Rs 5,500
- Full, 3 zones + LD2410 mmWave: ~Rs 8,000-8,500
- Full + power backup (router UPS, if not already at home): ~Rs 10,000-11,000 (estimate)
- Monthly cost: Rs 0 (Telegram alerts over the home WiFi are free; no
  subscription, no SIM, no mobile data). The system is WiFi-only: it runs on
  the existing home WiFi. A GSM add-on (SIM800L, +Rs 3,000) exists only as a
  future expansion if WiFi is ever unavailable; it is NOT part of the plan.
- Phase 2 (experimental): WiFi CSI — measuring a person's presence from the
  disturbance their body causes to the existing 2.4 GHz WiFi signal
  (frequency/amplitude change), using a second ESP32 (~Rs 1,200) as listener.
  Not built or verified without hardware; Phase 1 sensors are the reliable
  path. See firmware/wifi_csi_experiment/README.md.

## Honest limits (stated on the site itself)

- One sensor covers one zone only; every room needs its own sensor.
- Radar is not reliable through thick brick/concrete walls.
- PIR needs line of sight; fans, heaters and pets can cause false alarms.
- Power cut stops the system unless a router UPS / power bank is used. If the
  home WiFi/internet is down, Telegram alerts wait until WiFi returns; the
  siren and light still trigger locally.
- No system is 100% — strong doors, good locks and CCTV (as evidence) are still needed.
- The TikTok video that inspired the project was a Python simulation, not real
  sensor data; the site says so clearly. The dashboard DEMO MODE is also
  simulated and labelled as such.
- LD2410 price (Rs 1,200-1,800) is an unverified estimate; it is marked as
  such on the site.

## Verified (25 Nov 2026)

- ESP32 firmware compiles: PlatformIO 6.2.0, SUCCESS, RAM 14.7%, Flash 77.0%.
- Dashboard smoke test: 31/31 pass. Pin cross-check firmware vs wiring guide:
  14/14 match.
- Not verifiable without hardware: live sensor behaviour, LD2410 frame parsing
  against a real sensor, Telegram end-to-end delivery.
